name: Seed Germination & Propagation

objectives.text: Identify the parts of a seed, including the seed coat, embryo, and cotyledon
Plant seeds in a container and record observations of their growth into seedlings
Describe the stages a seed goes through as it germinates into a seedling
Compare how seeds are dispersed by wind, water, animals, and people
Investigate how water, temperature, and light affect whether seeds sprout in a simple class experiment
Explain the difference between growing a new plant from seed and growing one from a plant part such as a bulb, tuber, or runner
Explain the role of imbibition, temperature, and oxygen in triggering seed germination
Distinguish between epigeal and hypogeal germination and between monocot and dicot seedling emergence
Explain how seed dormancy works and how scarification and stratification break it
Demonstrate an asexual propagation technique such as taking and rooting a stem cutting
Identify the functions and components of seeds and how seed structure relates to planting and use
Identify common crop seedlings by their visual characteristics at emergence
Demonstrate sowing techniques, including correct depth, spacing, and media, that create favorable conditions for germination
Conduct a rag doll or germination chamber test to calculate seed germination percentage
Examine how seed age, storage conditions, moisture, and damage affect seed viability, vigor, and germination rates
Conduct viability and vigor tests such as a tetrazolium or cold test and interpret the results for planting decisions
Summarize the optimal conditions for rooting cuttings, including humidity, temperature, media, and rooting hormones
Demonstrate plant propagation by division, separation, layering, budding, and grafting
Compare sexual and asexual propagation methods for their advantages and uses in crop and nursery production
Assess how pre-plant treatments such as seed coatings, inoculants, fungicides, and priming affect germination and stand establishment
Evaluate how different seed and fruit structures influence seed handling, planting, and crop culture
Calculate a seeding rate from germination percentage and target plant population and recommend planter calibration to achieve it
Assess how mechanical planting equipment prepares the seedbed and places seed for uniform emergence
Evaluate the use of tissue culture and micropropagation for producing disease-free, genetically uniform plants at commercial scale
Design a propagation plan for a greenhouse or SAE enterprise that selects methods, schedules, and conditions to meet a production goal

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, rewording lightly and moving germination stages to grade 3 and propagation comparison to focus on crop and nursery uses. Added early hands-on planting, seed dispersal, simple germination experiments, and vegetative structures for elementary grades. Added dormancy, scarification and stratification, and emergence types for middle school. Added high school competencies tied to the AFNR standards: seed structure and function, seedling identification, sowing technique, germination, viability and vigor testing, optimal rooting conditions, the full range of asexual techniques, pre-plant treatments, seeding rate and planter calibration, planting equipment, and a capstone propagation plan for SAE or greenhouse work. Left PS.03.01.01.b (pollination) and PS.01.03.01.a (whole crop production cycle) unused because they belong to sibling or broader topics.
